claims.text: Debezium documents an initial consistent MySQL snapshot using repeatable-read semantics, records the current binlog position, and then streams changes from that position. The candidate correctly requires full-copy and incremental CDC to share one recoverable time boundary instead of copying first and opening the change stream later.

Debezium documents that replacement/restarted tasks can regenerate events already processed before a crash, and that a purged required binlog position can make the old position unavailable and require a new snapshot/baseline. The candidate therefore makes target writes idempotent and treats binlog retention as a hard recovery boundary.

MySQL 8.4 documents InnoDB DML as ACID transaction processing with commit, rollback and crash recovery. The candidate correctly keeps one-side database transaction guarantees separate from application dual-write across old and new storage topologies and does not claim those two writes become one atomic transaction.

MySQL 8.4 documents ALGORITHM and LOCK controls for online DDL, while operation tables show that concurrency and rebuild/copy behavior vary by operation. The candidate correctly says only some InnoDB DDL permits concurrent DML and explicitly avoids presenting online DDL as universally instant or lock-free.

Route epochs/fencing, shadow reads, batch pause thresholds, reverse synchronization during a rollback window, reconciliation, fault injection and virtual-bucket routing are presented as explicit scenario design choices rather than undocumented MySQL or Debezium guarantees. They consistently preserve the documented snapshot/CDC and transactional boundaries: stale writers must be fenced, application dual-write is not assumed atomic, and rollback after new-primary writes requires the old side to be current before routing back.

The candidate explicitly asks for production scale inputs and labels the 4 TiB at 200 MiB/s calculation as a hypothetical lower-bound example rather than a production fact. Its stated theoretical copy time of about 5.8 hours is arithmetically consistent, and it separately calls out CDC, verification, retries and peak throttling as additional planning cost.

findings: Both duplicate source rows are directly covered by the same explicit zero-downtime 16-to-64-table migration design.
The snapshot/binlog boundary, replay tolerance and purged-log recovery boundary are consistent with current Debezium MySQL documentation.

Cutover and rollback preserve a single write-authority model: old writers are fenced by route epoch, application dual-write is not claimed atomic, and routing back requires the old side to be current.
The MySQL 8.4 online-DDL wording is version-bounded and operation-dependent rather than universal.
The project section is a mapping prompt and explicitly hypothetical capacity example, not fabricated personal production experience.
